brief: One-sentence satirical roast of lawmakers who regulate AI/crypto/the internet but cannot convert a file to PDF. Criteria in order: (1) on-subject roast, (2) real turn: authority set up then undercut by the file, (3) aim stays on lawmakers and the rules they write, (4) reads clean in one pass, punch in the last few words, (5) specific unexpected detail, not a worn tech-illiteracy cliche.

pairs.reason: turn+detail: 400 pages of law vs a screenshot, punch 'the PDF button had defeated them' lands last
turn: 'tame artificial intelligence' vs 'on hold with IT' is a sharper authority drop
detail+turn: the explainability law itself is the setup; 'scanned it sideways' is the unexpected specific
detail: nine-year-old intern doing it in four seconds, punch lands on the last words
turn: they lost the vote's own minutes to the format — the act undercuts itself
aim+punch: v2 keeps the joke on the rules they write (400 pages of law) and its punch is more quotable
detail+turn: three-step escalation (printed, scanned sideways, photographed) beats one-step screenshot
